questions.qtext:
Consider a system that supports both user-level and Kernel-level threads using a many-to-many (M : N) mapping model.
Which of the following statements is TRUE for such a system?

options.text: Each user-level thread is always bound to a unique Kernel thread.
The OS scheduler schedules user-level threads directly.
Blocking of one user-level thread does not necessarily block the entire process.
All user-level threads in the same process share one Kernel thread.

questions.solution:
(c)
In an M : N mapping model, multiple user-level threads are multiplexed over multiple Kernel threads.
Hence, even if one user-level thread performs a blocking system call, other user threads can
continue execution via another Kernel thread thus, the M : N model improving concurrency and
enhances overall throughput of the process.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : In a demand paging system, a page is brought into memory only when it is referenced during execution.
S2 : Dynamic linking helps in reducing memory space usage by allowing multiple processes to share the same code.
S3 : Pages that are currently being shared by two or more active processes cannot be swapped out by the operating system.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
(a)
• In demand paging, pages are brought into main memory only when they are required by a
process. This reduces the initial loading time of programs and saves memory space.
Hence, the statement about programmer instruction is false, as the OS handles it automatically.
So, S1 is correct.
• Dynamic linking allows multiple processes to share the same copy of library routines in
memory. It avoids duplication and improves overall memory utilization efficiency. So, S2 is correct.
• Pages shared between processes can be swapped out if none of them are using those pages.
When needed again, they are simply brought back into memory by the OS.
Thus, the statement claiming they can never be swapped out is false. So, S3 is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: In a fixed-partition memory system, the worst-fit method can lead to internal fragmentation.
External fragmentation can occur in the best-fit and first-fit memory allocation methods, in variable partition scheme.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
• Both best-fit and first-fit methods use variable-sized partitions. Over time, free memory may
become divided into small scattered holes, resulting in external fragmentation. So, option (b) is correct.
• Compaction eliminates external fragmentation by moving allocated blocks together and
merging all free spaces into one large contiguous block. So, option (c) is correct
• Paging eliminates external fragmentation, not internal fragmentation. Because pages are of
fixed size, the last page of a process may not be completely filled, resulting in internal
fragmentation. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements about DMA (Direct Memory Access) is true?

options.text: In cycle stealing mode, the DMA controller transfers a complete block of data without releasing the bus.
DMA eliminates the need for CPU intervention during data transfer.
In burst mode DMA, CPU and DMA controller share the bus simultaneously.
DMA requires the CPU to execute an instruction for every byte transferred.

questions.solution:
(b)
• In cycle stealing mode, only one word is transferred at a time before releasing the bus.
Transferring an entire block without releasing the bus describes burst mode, not cycle stealing.
So, option (a) is incorrect
• Once initialized, DMA transfers data directly between memory and I/O without CPU help.
Thus, CPU intervention is not required during the transfer phase. So, option (b) is correct
• In burst mode, the DMA controller holds the bus exclusively until the entire block is transferred.
The CPU is temporarily suspended and cannot share the bus. So, option (c) is incorrect
• Requiring the CPU to execute an instruction for every byte is a property of Programmed I/O,
not DMA. DMA automates this process to save CPU time. So, option (d) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Technical
